# Vienna 1683 – Agriculture & food

- **Three-field rotation** [`three_field_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/three_field_system.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Villages of the Marchfeld, Tullnerfeld and Weinviertel farm in three fields under their lords. Tatar raiders burn much of the countryside in July 1683.
- **Legumes and green manure** [`legumes_green_manure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/legumes_green_manure.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Peas, beans, lentils and vetch are sown for food and fodder, seldom ploughed in. Sown clover is hardly known. Elsewhere: Flanders, Brabant and Lombardy: sown clover.
- **Four-course rotation with clover and turnips** [`crop_rotation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crop_rotation.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. The fallow is common pasture by village custom, so one farmer cannot sow it. A landlord could on his own demesne. Local: Hohberg's Georgica curiosa (Nuremberg 1682), the new handbook of Austrian estate farming. Elsewhere: Flanders and Brabant; described for the English by Weston (1650).
- **Manure, compost and night soil** [`manure_compost_night_soil`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/manure_compost_night_soil.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Stable dung goes to vineyards and gardens around the city; cesspit contents are a nuisance, not a ware. In the siege neither can be carted out.
- **Liming and marling of sour soils** [`liming_marling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/liming_marling.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Known from the Roman authors and Hohberg. Much of the land round Vienna is chalky loess that does not need it.
- **Mineral fertiliser (guano, phosphate, potash, nitrate)** [`mineral_fertiliser`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mineral_fertiliser.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Ash and bone are used by custom without theory. Saltpetre earth goes to the powder mills, not the fields.
- **Terracing and soil conservation** [`terracing_soil_conservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/terracing_soil_conservation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: dry-stone vineyard terraces of the Wachau.

- **Seed drill** [`seed_drill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/seed_drill.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Sowing machines appear in Italian books and patents (Torello, Venice 1566); none is used here. Seed is broadcast by hand; labour is cheap, seed dear.
- **Scythe and grain cradle** [`scythe_cradle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scythe_cradle.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Austrian scythes are an export ware, used for hay. Bread grain is cut with the sickle to save the ears; a cradle on the scythe is not used. Elsewhere: scythe smiths of Kirchdorf-Micheldorf and Waidhofen an der Ybbs.

- **Selective breeding of plants and animals** [`selective_breeding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selective_breeding.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Court studs breed horses by pedigree; peasants' cattle and sheep mate on the common pasture. Results take years. Elsewhere: imperial studs at Lipica (1580) and Kladrub (1579).

- **Irrigation and water lifting (canal, qanat, shaduf, noria)** [`irrigation_water_lifting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/irrigation_water_lifting.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Rain suffices for field crops. Gardens are watered from wells with buckets and windlasses, and mill races are common.
- **Wet rice (paddy) cultivation** [`wet_rice_cultivation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wet_rice_cultivation.md) — K2, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Rice is bought from Lombardy through Venice as a food for the well-off and for fast days. Nobody grows it north of the Alps.
- **Polders – land reclamation with dikes and wind pumps** [`windmill_drainage_land_reclamation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill_drainage_land_reclamation.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept medium. Dutch polders are known from travellers and engineers' books. The Danube floodplain is left as hunting ground, pasture and firewood; mills here are water mills and ship mills. Elsewhere: Holland: Beemster polder (1612).
- **Fish ponds and carp polyculture** [`aquaculture_fish_ponds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aquaculture_fish_ponds.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. Carp for the many fast days comes live from the ponds of southern Bohemia and the Waldviertel. None reaches the city during the siege. Elsewhere: Wittingau (Třeboň) pond systems.
- **Crops of the Americas (potato, maize and others)** [`new_world_crops`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/new_world_crops.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Beans and pumpkins are ordinary and tobacco is smoked everywhere. Maize (Türkischer Weizen, Kukuruz) is grown in Hungary and the south, not round Vienna. Tomato and potato are rarities.
- **Growing and storing potatoes** [`potato_cultivation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/potato_cultivation.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Clusius had tubers in Vienna in 1588, and Abbot Plautz of Seitenstetten printed potato recipes at Linz in 1621. It remains a curiosity of monastery and noble gardens. Local: Stift Seitenstetten (Lower Austria); noble and monastery gardens. Elsewhere: Ireland: a field crop.
- **Maize, beans and squash grown together (milpa)** [`maize_beans_squash_milpa`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/maize_beans_squash_milpa.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. All three plants are available as seed, but maize is sown alone like a grain.
- **Nixtamalisation (lime treatment of maize)** [`nixtamalisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nixtamalisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Maize is ground and boiled as porridge. Where it is only one food among several no harm shows, so nobody sees a reason to steep it in lime.

- **The Columbian exchange (plants, animals and diseases across the Atlantic)** [`columbian_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/columbian_exchange.md) — K2, use partial, make very-hard, accept medium. Scholars know which plants came from the Indies and argue whether the French disease did. Common names credit the Turks instead: Türkischer Weizen.
- **Food preservation (salting, drying, smoking, pickling)** [`food_preservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_preservation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Salt meat, smoked bacon, sauerkraut, dried fruit, biscuit and wine fill the cellars. The city has no serious supply failure in the siege; fresh meat and prices are the trouble. Local: Oberkämmerer Daniel Fockhy and Jakob Daniel Tepser, who oversee the distribution of provisions.
- **Canning (heat-preserving in sealed containers)** [`canning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/canning.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Glass bottles, corks, wax and kettles exist; tinplate canisters do not. A spoiled or burst bottle would end the trial.
- **Pasteurisation** [`pasteurisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pasteurisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Vintners sulphur their casks and know that wine turns in summer. Heating it gently on purpose would seem to ruin it.
- **Grain storage and protection from pests and ergot** [`grain_storage_pest_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grain_storage_pest_control.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Grain lies in lofts and magazines and is turned with shovels against heat and weevils. Ergot in rye is milled along; the Paris findings of the 1670s are unknown. Local: city and court granaries; bakers and mills (ship mills on the Danube lie outside the walls).
- **Sea fisheries – stockfish, salt cod and cured herring** [`sea_fisheries_salt_cod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sea_fisheries_salt_cod.md) — K3, use partial, make impossible, accept high. Stockfish and barrelled herring are bought for Lent through the German trading towns. Vienna is far from any sea.
- **Sugar from cane and from beet** [`sugar_cane_beet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sugar_cane_beet.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept high. Cane sugar is sold by apothecaries and confectioners as loaves from Venice, Hamburg and Amsterdam. That beet holds the same sugar is unknown; honey is the common sweetener.
- **Sericulture (silk raising)** [`sericulture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sericulture.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Becher's Werkhaus on the Tabor housed a silk manufactory in the 1670s; it failed against guild opposition and burns in 1683. Raw silk is bought from Italy. Elsewhere: Lombardy, Veneto, Lyon.
- **Movable-frame beehive** [`beekeeping_movable_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/beekeeping_movable_frame.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Bees are kept in straw skeps and log hives and often killed with sulphur at harvest. Wax is in heavy demand for church candles.
- **Coffee, tea and cacao** [`coffee_tea_cacao`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coffee_tea_cacao.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept high. Coffee is known from Ottoman embassies and Armenian merchants. No public coffee house exists until Johannes Diodato's privilege of 17 January 1685; Kolschitzky as founder is a later legend. Local: Armenian merchants; Johannes Diodato (Armenian merchant and imperial courier). Elsewhere: coffee houses in Venice, London, Oxford, Paris, Hamburg; the Ottoman camp, where the captive Marsigli serves as coffee cook.
